title: SSE fragment merging and session safepoint protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several customers reported truncated or duplicated tokens when an SSE connection dropped mid-response and the client reconnected quickly. Existing resume heuristics sometimes left orphaned fragments in the server merge window, producing duplicate partial outputs or missing suffix tokens. This ticket implements a deterministic fragment-merge protocol using a session safepoint token to guarantee continuity without requiring full request replay.
customer_reports: MetaHealth TKT-8732: intermittent missing tail tokens on long streaming completions (avg 2.1% of streams during peak)
EduFlow TKT-8790: duplicated sentence fragments when clients auto-reconnect within 200ms
internal-observation: error spike correlated with region-eu-1 connection churn on 2026-03-10
reproduce_steps: Open SSE connection to POST /v1/streams with stream_id header and sequence numbers enabled
Send prompt that produces >1024 tokens so server sends multiple fragments/chunks
Force a TCP close mid-fragment (client disconnect) and immediately reconnect with same stream_id and session safepoint token
Observe duplicated fragments or missing suffix in the reconstructed stream on the client SDKs (node/python) when server merge rules accept both fragments
investigation_notes: Server keeps fragments in an in-memory merge window keyed by stream_id + sequence_range. When reconnects are fast, both the original partial fragment and the reconnect fragment overlap and the merge function is non-deterministic.
KV cache interaction: reconnections occasionally replay tokens from KV cache leading to repeated suffixes when fragment boundaries don't align with cache checkpoints.
Observed cases where client reconnects with slightly different sequence offsets due to client-side buffering; server accepted reconnects without a safepoint validation.
Heap and latency impact minimal for merge-window TTL of 10s, but correctness is broken under race.
root_cause: Lack of a deterministic safepoint token and strict merge policy allowed overlapping fragments to be merged twice. Merge logic assumed fragment alignment that doesn't hold under quick reconnects and certain client buffering behaviors.
short_term_mitigation: Deploy feature-flagged hotfix that introduces an idempotency marker per fragment (fragment_id = stream_id + fragment_start_ts) and deduplicates by marker
Increase merge-window TTL to 20s for affected regions to give clients more time to reconcile (temporary)
Notify top affected customers with recommended client SDK patch that waits 300ms before aggressive reconnects
long_term_fix: Implement session safepoint token: server returns safepoint after each acknowledged fragment; clients must present safepoint on reconnect to assert last-consumed offset
Replace best-effort merge with a deterministic merge rule: accept only non-overlapping fragments or fragments that explicitly reference a safepoint bridging them
Add merge-window metrics and histograms (fragment overlap rate, duplicate-fragment drops) and alert when overlap_rate > 0.1%
Extend SDKs to automatically handle safepoint tokens and exponential reconnect backoff with jitter
rollout_plan: 1) Canary hotfix to compute fragment_id and drop duplicates (region-us-west-2) — immediate (hotpatch)
2) Feature-flagged safepoint protocol server implementation behind runtime flag — deploy to staging
3) SDK updates (node/python/go) to include safepoint handling and backoff — ship with minor version bump
4) Enable safepoint protocol in canaries and run 72h compare against baseline metrics (error_rate, duplicate_fragments)
5) Full rollout to hosted regions with coordinated customer notifications and migration guide
telemetry_queries: SELECT region, count(*) AS dup_fragments FROM stream_fragments WHERE duplicate_flag = true AND ts >= now() - interval '7 days' GROUP BY region ORDER BY dup_fragments DESC;
acceptance_criteria: No customer reproductions for TKT-8732 and TKT-8790 after hotfix for 72h
Merge-window metrics show duplicate-fragment drops reduced to <0.001 of streams in canary region
SDKs automatically surface safepoint token and reconnect flow documented in Console docs
Load test with 50k concurrent streams shows <1% latency regression at 95th percentile after safepoint enabled
